[Date]

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

**Re: October 27, 2026 — Amara Okafor, Bus 41, Route 9**

I am writing in response to your complaint dated October 29 regarding Amara’s afternoon bus ride on Tuesday, October 27. My supervisor, Darlene, provided the complaint to me on November 3 and asked me to submit a written statement. Because this statement will be included in my file and a copy provided to you, I want to give a clear account of what happened and address your concerns directly.

I understand that you were frightened and upset when Amara did not get off the bus as you expected. As a grandparent, I can understand how upsetting it would be not to know immediately where a young child was going. I am sorry for the worry and difficult afternoon you experienced. At the same time, I want to explain why I kept Amara on the bus and returned her to Fairmont Elementary. My decision was based on the district’s kindergarten release rule and my responsibility to keep her safely supervised.

On October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on the Route 9 elementary afternoon run. Amara’s stop was at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. The scheduled arrival time was 3:50 p.m., and I arrived at approximately 3:52 p.m. I remained at the stop until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I did not see an adult waiting to receive Amara at the corner.

Amara is a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary and has a green tag on her bag indicating that an adult must be present at the stop for her release. Under the district rule for kindergarten riders, if no adult is present to receive the child, the child remains on the bus and is returned to school, where the office contacts the parent. Because I could not see an adult there to receive Amara, I followed that procedure rather than allowing her to get off the bus.

At approximately 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school. I still had three stops to complete and 14 children remaining on the bus. I continued the route before returning Amara to Fairmont Elementary. We arrived at the school at approximately 4:31 p.m. I personally walked Amara inside and placed her in the care of Mrs. Petrakis in the school office.

I understand from your account that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and waved to me. I did not see you or your wave. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street, although I cannot say for certain whether it blocked my view of you. I do not dispute that you were there or that you tried to get my attention. I can only state what I observed from the driver’s seat: I did not see an adult whom I could identify as being there to receive Amara.

I did not knowingly ignore you or refuse to respond. Had I seen your wave, I would have had an opportunity to determine who was there to receive her. Without seeing you, however, I could not safely assume that an adult was waiting nearby. I also could not leave the children unattended on the bus while I got off to look across the street or check parked vehicles. My responsibility at that point was to keep Amara and the other children supervised and follow the return-to-school procedure.

I also want to address the statement that I “drove off laughing.” I was not laughing. As we pulled away, I was directing a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down. That was the interaction taking place at the front of the bus at that time. I was not making light of Amara’s situation or your concern.

During the remainder of the ride, Amara appeared comfortable. She was coloring on her folder and asked whether she could ride more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip. My intention was to reassure her while I completed the route and returned her to school. I mention her behavior to describe what I observed, not to minimize the worry you experienced. I understand that her appearing comfortable on the bus would not have relieved your concern when you did not yet know what was happening.

I respectfully request that the transportation office promptly preserve and review the available bus camera footage from that afternoon. The review should include our arrival at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, the time spent waiting, our departure, and the remainder of Amara’s ride through the return to Fairmont Elementary, to the extent those events were recorded. If audio is available, I ask that it also be reviewed, particularly the interaction as we left the stop. I would like the complaint and this statement considered alongside the available recording so that the record is as complete and accurate as possible.

I have driven a school bus for 28 years without a write-up. I take that responsibility seriously, especially when transporting children who are too young to be released without an adult. I include my work history as context for the care I bring to this job, while recognizing that this incident should be reviewed on its own facts.

Going forward, I respectfully ask that you wait where I can clearly see you, preferably on the bus side of the street where it is safe to do so, or step out of your parked car so I can identify you before releasing Amara. I would welcome the transportation office’s help in confirming a safe, visible waiting location so that we both know what to expect at pickup.

I am glad to continue driving Amara, and I want our daily contact to be respectful and comfortable. My purpose in writing is not to place blame, but to explain that I returned her to school because I did not see an adult at the stop and followed the district’s required procedure. I hope this account, together with a review of the footage, helps resolve your concerns and allows us to move forward with a clear understanding.

Sincerely,

[Driver’s Name]  
Bus 41, Route 9  
[School District / Transportation Department]

cc: Darlene, Transportation Supervisor  
Transportation Office
